problem:
A particle $P$ of mass $4\,\text{kg}$ is subject to the external forces 

$$
{F}_{1}=⟨8\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,4\operatorname{ln}⁡(t+1)⟩,\,{F}_{2}=⟨12-8\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,10-4\operatorname{ln}⁡(t+1)⟩,
$$

where ${F}_{1}$ and ${F}_{2}$ are measured in newtons and $t>0$ is the time, in seconds. Given that the velocity of $P$ equals $⟨1,\,-1⟩\,\text{m/s}$ when $t=0\,\text{s},$ calculate the speed of $P$ when $t=3\,\text{s}.$ Do not round the answer.

The speed of $P$ when $t=3\,\text{s}$ is
{{field-1}}
$\text{m/s}.$

activity_context.topic_title: Applying Newton's Second Law in the Plane

feedback.problem:
A particle $P$ of mass $3\,\text{kg}$ is subject to the external forces 

$$
{F}_{1}=⟨6{e}^{t},\,\frac{9}{t+2}⟩,\,{F}_{2}=⟨3-6{e}^{t},\,1-\frac{9}{t+2}⟩,
$$

where ${F}_{1}$ and ${F}_{2}$ are measured in newtons and $t>0$ is the time, in seconds. Given that the velocity of $P$ equals $⟨-2,\,0⟩\,\text{m/s}$ when $t=0\,\text{s},$ calculate the speed of $P$ when $t=\frac{1}{2}\,\text{s}.$ Do not round the answer.

The speed of $P$ when $t=\frac{1}{2}\,\text{s}$ is
{{field-1}}
$\text{m/s}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
Newton's second law states that

$$
F=ma,
$$

where $F$ is the *resultant* force, $m$ is the mass, and $a$ is the acceleration.

The resultant force $F$ acting on $P$ equals the sum of the forces acting on $P.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F & ={F}_{1}+{F}_{2} \\  & =⟨6{e}^{t},\,\frac{9}{t+2}⟩+⟨3-6{e}^{t},\,1-\frac{9}{t+2}⟩ \\  & =⟨3,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

By Newton's second law, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{F}{m} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\cdot ⟨3,\,1⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,\frac{1}{3}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

To compute the velocity vector $v,$ we need to integrate the acceleration vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\int a\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int ⟨1,\,\frac{1}{3}⟩\,\text{d}t \\  & =⟨\int 1\,\text{d}t,\,\int \frac{1}{3}\,\text{d}t⟩ \\  & =⟨t,\,\frac{1}{3}t⟩+C\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is a (vector) constant of integration. 

We can solve for $C$ by substituting $v=⟨-2,\,0⟩\,\text{m/s}$ and $t=0\,\text{s}$ into the above, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨-2,\,0⟩ & =⟨0,\,\frac{1}{3}(0)⟩+C \\ ⟨-2,\,0⟩ & =⟨0,\,0⟩+C \\ C & =⟨-2,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity of $P$ at time $t$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =⟨t,\,\frac{1}{3}t⟩+⟨-2,\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨t-2,\,\frac{1}{3}t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

When $t=\frac{1}{2},$ the velocity equals

$$
\begin{aligned}v\,(\frac{1}{2}) & =⟨\frac{1}{2}-2,\,\frac{1}{3}\cdot \frac{1}{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{3}{2},\,\frac{1}{6}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the speed of $P$ when $t=\frac{1}{2}$ equals the magnitude of $v\,(\frac{1}{2}).$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}|v\,(\frac{1}{2})| & =\sqrt{{(-\frac{3}{2})}^{2}+{(\frac{1}{6})}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{82}}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the speed of $P$ when $t=\frac{1}{2}\,\text{s}$ is $\frac{\sqrt{82}}{6}\,\text{m/s}.$
